propositions: Production in-process verifier achieved 100% per-AC agreement with ground truth (65/65) and zero rejections on real ACs across the corpus.
Minimal free-tool harness agent (Arm B) achieved 94.6% agreement (87/92) with 5 false-FAILs on real epic ACs despite zero false-PASSes on planted ACs.
Arm B median wall time (415.5 s) exceeded 2× Arm A median wall time (131 s), violating the predeclared performance threshold.
The five Arm B rejections concentrated on epic AC7 (stamp/mapping mutation commit claim) and AC2 (enrichment data assertion), representing defensible strict readings rather than tooling constraints.

Operator hypothesis that in-process scaffolding unreliability motivates external-harness design is not supported; Arm A control verifier showed no false-FAILs and no evidence-insufficient verdicts on this corpus.
